predeclaration.note: Written before any R3_scen number was computed. Descriptive atlas: nothing is selected or tuned.
definitions: net = executable time-exit return open[t+1]->close[t+h] (adjusted) minus 50 bps, for every label; barrier-exit P&L also reported for barrier labels
triple barrier: ATR multiples (2.0/2.0) and (3.0/1.5) scaled by sqrt(h/20), next-open entry, stop checked first, time-exit dead zone +-50 bps; touch shares cross-checked vs atlas_v2
XR_neu / XR_neumom: exact R2_rel recipe on the elig_base peer group, classes 30/40/30; cross-checked vs results/R2_rel/labels_h*.npz
DUAL built on the frozen label XR_neumom: +1 = top-30% AND r>+50bps; -1 = bottom-30% AND r<-50bps; else 0
old repo label = atlas_v2 definition (raw close[t]->raw close[t+h] > 0 within segment, NaN->0), evaluated on every row of the filter (valid window or not)
filters choose sample rows only; relative labels keep their elig_base rank inside liq5 / F&O / gates
VIX terciles ex-ante: India VIX percentile within its trailing 252 trading days
extra_variants: 1: 'none' filter for relative/DUAL labels re-ranked among all valid rows (missing regressors -> per-date median)
2: PROD avoid tail (bottom 30%) excess vs universe by scenario
3: same-window market correlation of the daily +1 share (in addition to atlas-style monthly corr)

columns: Up share on a weak day (5th percentile of days)
Up share on a strong day (95th percentile of days)
Correlation of daily up share with the market's own 20-day return
Average net return when labelled up
Average net return when labelled down (−1, or 0 for two-class labels)
Chance an 'up' row actually made money

up/down barrier at 2.0×ATR×√(h/20), first touch wins; time exit ±0.5% dead zone
target 3.0×ATR, stop 1.5×ATR (×√(h/20)); time exit ±0.5% dead zone
rank of risk-adjusted return vs same-day peers (beta, volatility, size neutral): top 30% / middle / bottom 30%
as XR_neu but also momentum-neutral (12-1 month); the team's frozen label
+1 only if top-30% relative AND return > +0.5%; −1 only if bottom-30% AND < −0.5%
html_tables.note: Tradable universe = elig_base (EQ series, price ≥ ₹20, ≥ ₹2 cr daily turnover, seasoned, not circuit-locked). Net return = buy at next day's open, sell at the close 20 trading days later, minus 0.5% round-trip cost. A label whose up share swings from ~13% to ~83% of stocks and moves 0.7-0.9 with the market is mostly describing the market, not the stock. The relative labels hold exactly 30% up every day by construction. Absolute labels' 'up' P&L is high by construction (the class is defined by the outcome); what matters is what can be predicted in advance (table 7).

html_tables.title: 2. What is wrong with the old repo label, measured (tradable universe, 2021-2026)
columns: Rows labelled 'not up' only because the future price is missing
Share of the old label's 'not up' class that is really 'unknown'
Rows labelled although the clean window is invalid (suspension/corporate-action break)
Rows where unadjusted prices flip the sign vs adjusted prices
Fake crashes from splits/bonuses (raw < −30%, adjusted > −10%), count
Rows where the old label disagrees with the clean sign label
Average return if you could buy at the signal close (not possible)
Average return buying at the next open (what you can actually do)
Phantom return per trade (close entry minus open entry)
Median executable return (a typical stock loses money before costs)
html_tables.note: The old label is close to the clean sign label on most rows (3-6% disagree) but it is biased: missing futures are counted as 'not up', raw prices create fake split crashes, and the close entry adds ~26 bps per trade that no one can trade. The old label is evaluated on every row (valid future or not), exactly as the repo did; within-entity windows make this a kinder version than the repo's ticker-keyed shift.

html_tables.title: 3. Event rates by holding period (tradable universe, 2021-2026)
columns: Corr. with market return over the same window
Corr. with market (monthly, old atlas method)
html_tables.note: Longer horizons do not make absolute labels less market-driven: the same-window correlation stays 0.85-0.88 for the sign labels at every horizon. The monthly method used in earlier rounds understates it at 20 days (0.47) because a 20-day window straddles two calendar months. Relative labels stay at 30% up and ≈0 market correlation at every horizon. The 3-class flat share shrinks from 9% (5 days) to 4% (20 days) because 20-day moves rarely stay inside ±0.5%.

columns: Filter (used only to choose which stocks are considered)
Share of trading days the filter fires

html_tables.note: Filters never change a label's value; they only choose rows. Relative labels keep their rank among the tradable universe, so an up share above 30% means the filter tends to select relative winners (trend +3.3 pp, washout +1.7 pp). For 'No filter' the relative labels are re-ranked among all stocks (they are undefined otherwise). The washout gate fires on ~16% of days only.

columns: Clean sign: average net when up
Clean sign: average net when not up
XR_neumom: chance a +1 stock made money
rows: No filter (every stock with a valid 20-day future)

html_tables.note: Class separation (up vs down P&L) survives every filter. Liquid and F&O names have smaller spreads (they move less); the unfiltered universe has the widest spread but includes untradable rows (BE series, < ₹20, illiquid, circuit-locked).

html_tables.title: 6. Scenarios × labels at 20 days (tradable universe, 2021-2026): how the market backdrop changes the event rates
columns: Scenario (first 9 rows known on the signal day; last 4 known only afterwards)
Average net return of all stocks
Clean sign: chance an 'up' row made money
XR_neumom: chance a +1 stock made money
html_tables.note: Ex-ante states (200-day average, 20-day momentum, breadth, VIX tercile vs its own past year) move the absolute up share only between 0.44 and 0.58; the realised market move (ex-post rows) moves it from 0.14 to 0.78. The relative label stays at 30% in every scenario, but its absolute payoff does not: when the market falls more than 5% over the next 20 days, the top-30% stocks average only about +0.8% net and fewer than half make money. Overlapping 20-day windows: there are only 64 independent 20-day periods in 2021-2026 (labelled days / 20), so scenario differences are descriptive, not tradable rules.

html_tables.title: 7. The tradable version: frozen PROD score by scenario (top-20 picks vs the whole universe, 20-day hold)
columns: DEV: rank IC with the label
html_tables.note: Each signal day: top-20 by PROD (walk-forward, never trained on the day it scores), bought next open, sold 20 days later, minus 0.5%. Universe = all tradable stocks equally weighted (also minus 0.5%). This is a per-day signal study (overlapping trades), not the staggered book; R3_book has the book numbers. In 2023-25 the top-20 beat the universe in every ex-ante state; in 2026 the edge is about zero in most states although the rank IC (0.06) is intact - the long book does not monetise the IC. 2026 is reported, never used to choose.

html_tables.title: 8. Why 20 days: a random 20-stock book by holding period and trading cost (phase-averaged, 5 random seeds)
columns: Cost drag per year at 0.5% (0.5% × 252 / h)
html_tables.note: No skill at all, only the holding period changes: at 5 days a random book loses ~17%/yr to costs, at 20 days it makes ~12%/yr (2023-25). Every number is averaged over the 5 possible weekly start days. Stocks are total-return adjusted; Nifty 500 is a price index (≈1.2%/yr dividends missing). 2026 = Jan to mid-Oct, annualised.

html_tables.title: 9. Where Indian stock returns happen: overnight gap vs trading session (equal-weight tradable universe)
columns: Share of days the overnight gap is positive
Share of days the session is positive
html_tables.note: Equal-weight averages, re-balanced daily, before costs: not a tradable strategy (a daily round trip costs ~0.5%, more than the ~0.2-0.3% average gap). The pattern holds in every liquidity third, so it is not only an illiquid-stock artefact; part of it may be how NSE's open (auction / first trade) and close (last-30-minute average) prints are formed. Its practical meaning: a signal computed at the close can only be bought at the next open, after the gap has already been paid.

report_md:
# R3_scen: scenario and event-rate atlas (label explainer for the client)

Agent R3_scen. Scripts: s1_labels.py (label zoo), s2_atlas.py (zoo, filters, scenarios, PROD by scenario), s3_horizon.py
(horizon economics, overnight split), s4_tables.py (client tables and charts). Numbers live in results.json. Tables are in
section `html_tables`: t1 to t10, as fractions. Charts are in section `charts` (9). Key figures are in `key_numbers`. The
pre-declaration was saved to results.json (`predeclaration`) before any number was computed. The harness does not allow a
subagent to write a REPORT.md file, so this text is stored in results.json section `report_md` instead.

## What was done (descriptive atlas: nothing selected or tuned)
* Eight label definitions at h = 5/10/15/20 on the tradable universe (elig_base): the old repo label, clean sign,
  cost-aware 3-class (+-50 bps), triple barrier 2.0/2.0 and 3.0/1.5 (ATR x sqrt(h/20), time-exit dead zone +-50 bps),
  XR_neu, XR_neumom (frozen) and DUAL (frozen relative label AND |r| > 50 bps in the same direction).
* Seven filters at h=20: none, elig_base, liq5, F&O proxy, trend gate, washout gate (R2 A1), high delivery.
* Thirteen scenarios at h=20: 9 known in advance (Nifty 500 vs its 200-dma; 20-day market momentum; breadth50; VIX tercile
  vs its own trailing year) and 4 known only afterwards (realised Nifty 500 return over the next 20 days).
* The frozen PROD score by scenario (top-20 net, excess vs universe, avoid tail, rank IC), DEV and 2026.
* Horizon economics: phase-averaged 5-seed random 20-stock books by h x cost; overnight vs intraday split; the overnight tax.
* Cross-checks: XR_neu/XR_neumom reproduce R2_rel's files within 3e-8 at h=10/15/20. XR_neumom h20 is bit-exact with the
  devil's frozen label (max diff 0.0). Class shares, barrier touch shares and execution means reproduce atlas_v2. Random-book
  CAGRs agree with atlas_v2 (which used 3 seeds and one phase).

## Answers to the client's questions
1. Is the old repo label right? No. It agrees with the clean sign label on most rows: they disagree on 3.0% of rows at
   20 days and 5.5% at 5 days. But it is biased in three measurable ways (t2):
   * 1.97% of rows are labelled "not up" only because the future price is missing. That is 3.8% of its "not up" class.
   * Unadjusted prices flip the sign on 0.59% of rows, including 4,261 fake split/bonus "crashes" at 20 days.
   * Entering at the signal close is impossible. That phantom adds about 26 bps per trade: 1.33% vs 1.07% average 20-day
     return.
   Above all, it is a market label (point 2).
2. What do absolute labels measure? Mostly the market. The clean-sign 20-day up share averages 49.1% (DEV 50.7%, 2026
   48.7%), but it swings from 13.3% of stocks on a weak day to 82.9% on a strong day (5th/95th percentiles; sd 0.217).
   It correlates 0.876 with the market's own return over the same window. The monthly method used in earlier rounds shows
   only 0.468 at h=20, because a 20-day window straddles two calendar months; the same-window measure is the right one.
   Barrier labels are 0.71 to 0.72. A longer horizon does not reduce this.
3. Relative labels: 30% up every day by construction, with same-window market correlation 0.066 (XR_neumom, h=20). The
   classes separate P&L strongly: +12.2% net for +1 vs -9.3% for -1, and 90.4% of +1 rows made money. But the absolute
   payoff of a relative winner depends on the market. When the market falls more than 5% over the next 20 days, +1 rows
   average only +0.76% net and 43.9% make money. When it rises more than 5%, they average +20.1%.
4. DUAL ("both conditions") brings the market back. Its up share is 27.2% on average, but it varies daily (sd 0.056) and
   correlates 0.70 with the market.
5. Filters (conditions) change who is sampled, not what the label means. The up share of XR_neumom inside each filter
   shows whether the filter picks relative winners:
   * Trend gate 33.3%, washout 31.7%, high delivery 30.6%, F&O proxy 29.5% (vs 30% in the tradable universe).
   * The washout gate's rows average +2.89% net over 20 days (DEV +2.32%, 2026 +5.32%), but it fires on only 15.7% of days.
   * The tradable universe averages +0.91% net per 20-day trade in DEV.
   * Class separation survives every filter.
6. Scenarios. Known-in-advance states move the clean-sign up share only between 0.44 (VIX mid tercile) and 0.58 (Nifty
   below its 200-dma). The realised market move takes it from 0.14 (next 20 days < -5%) to 0.78 (> +5%). Most of an
   absolute label's variation is therefore unknowable at the signal date. There are only 64 independent 20-day periods,
   so scenario differences are descriptive, not rules.
7. The tradable version (PROD, t7). In DEV the top-20 beat the equal-weight universe by 1.33% per 20-day trade (NW t 4.89).
   It was positive in every known-in-advance state (smallest t 2.47). Only in the crash bin is the gain insignificant
   (+0.33%). In 2026 the excess is +0.11% (t 0.24) although the rank IC is intact (0.067 DEV, 0.063 2026). The avoid tail
   is -0.65% (t -4.30) in DEV and -0.30% (t -1.25) in 2026. In 2026 the avoid tail beat the universe in the strong-rally
   bin (+1.71%): junk rallies are the avoid side's weak spot.
8. Why 20 days (t8). With no skill at all, a random 20-stock book at 0.5% cost makes -16.8%/yr at 5 days, +1.3% at 10,
   +8.6% at 15 and +12.0% at 20 (DEV). In 2026 the figures are -20.6% at 5 days and +10.2% at 20. At 0.8% cost, the
   20-day book still makes +8.0%. For comparison, the Nifty 500 price index made 15.5%/yr in DEV and -9.9% annualised in
   2026 (it is a price index, so dividends are missing).
9. The overnight tax (t9, t10). The equal-weight universe earns its return overnight: +94.6%/yr from close to open vs
   -36.0%/yr from open to close in DEV (2026: +55.0% vs -28.4%). This holds in the most liquid third too (+71.5% vs
   -27.6%). A next-open entry gives up about 0.27% per trade. That is 15.5% of the close-entry return at 20 days but 59.2%
   at 5 days, or a 3.4%/yr drag vs 13.4%/yr if you re-enter every h days. The gap cannot be harvested, because a daily
   round trip costs more than it earns.

## Pros
* One reproducible build, cross-checked bit-exact against the frozen label and round-2 files.
* The same-window correlation corrects an understatement in the earlier atlas.
* Ex-ante and ex-post scenarios are kept separate. PROD-by-scenario shows where the edge lived (DEV, all states) and where
  it failed (2026).
* Client tables carry plain-language titles and notes.

## Cons / caveats
* Scenario and filter cells use overlapping 20-day windows (64 independent periods). The t-stats are not adjusted for
  multiplicity across 13 states x 2 periods.
* PROD-by-scenario is a per-day signal study (overlapping trades, equal weight, no sleeves), so it is not comparable with
  book CAGRs. R3_book owns the book numbers.
* Ex-post labels are coherent by construction; "mean net | up" says nothing about predictability.
* The old label here is the kinder within-entity version; the repo's ticker-keyed shift is worse.
* For the "none" filter, relative labels are re-ranked among all valid rows (extra variant 1), so they are not the frozen
  label.
* The overnight/intraday split depends on how NSE forms its open (auction/first trade) and close (last-30-minute VWAP)
  prices.
* 2026 is lightly contaminated and only reported. DEV event-rate stats use windows that end by 2025-12-31.
* VIX terciles are relative to India VIX's own trailing year.

## Variants
80 label x horizon x filter configurations: 8 labels x 4 horizons on elig_base, plus 8 labels x 6 other filters at h=20.
Extra variants declared in advance: (1) re-ranked relative labels for "none"; (2) PROD avoid tail by scenario; (3)
same-window market correlation. Descriptive cells: 13 scenarios x 8 labels x 3 periods; PROD 14 states x 2 periods;
random books 4 h x 3 costs x 2 periods, plus EW 4 h x 2 periods. No add-on was tested or adopted (not in this mandate).

variants.definition: 8 labels x 4 horizons on elig_base + 8 labels x 6 other filters at h=20
